question.text: Falcon Alpha Fund's equity-long-short team is preparing for IC. The PM argues that since Indian listed equities are in 'semi-strong form', fundamental analysis of annual reports and earnings calls WILL consistently beat the Nifty. Evaluate his claim.

answer.text: Correct - semi-strong form specifically rewards fundamental research and historical chart reading.
Correct - semi-strong form only rules out insider information, so public fundamentals still work.
Incorrect - semi-strong form says only technical analysis fails; fundamentals give alpha.
Incorrect - semi-strong form already assumes prices reflect all PUBLIC information (including fundamentals), so fundamental analysis alone cannot generate consistent risk-adjusted alpha.

explanation.text: The Logic: Semi-strong form efficiency states that prices reflect all historical and publicly available information. Under this assumption, public-information fundamental analysis cannot, on its own, generate consistent superior risk-adjusted returns. The Trap: Options A, B and C misstate the semi-strong hierarchy by preserving a fundamental-analysis edge or restricting the failure to technical analysis only. Note: Source pages 50-52 of FINAL Series XIX-C AIF Managers (Dec 2025) workbook.
